name: MLW Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The promotion's own top championship, changing hands three times by screwjob or scaffold across its first seven months.

name: MLW Canadian Heritage Championship
epitaph: A mid-card championship the promotion's own broadcasts named inconsistently across the year, but tracked as a single lineage here for want of any document splitting it in two.

name: MLW Northern Hardcore Championship
epitaph: Defended with no rules in a baseball stadium's own equipment rooms.

name: MLW True North Championship
epitaph: Filled from vacancy in a Royal Rumble and changed hands again inside a fortnight.

name: MLW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Awarded from vacancy to the winner of a five-team hotel-bar brawl.

name: CCWA World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The shared prize of a three-federation alliance, its first champion crowned in a match that left both finalists unable to stand.
notes: Sanctioned by the three federations' own joint alliance, self-named in its broadcasts' own closing copyright line ('"A World Of Pain" is (C) 1999 of the Coast to Coast Wrestling Alliance') and spelled out by member on a separate contemporaneous newsgroup post the same year ('the Coast to Coast Wrestling Alliance [GLCW/MLW/LWC]') to distinguish it from an unrelated same-acronym startup. Housed under this promotion's own shard because its own on-screen president is the surviving record's one individual production credit ('Day One was produced by "Hollywood" Chris Hebert (MLW)'); crossover-booking edges already link this promotion to both other members, and a frontier row records the alliance itself.

name: MLW Maple Leaf Championship
epitaph: Unveiled by the promotion's executive vice president as the prize of the Maplemania 2 opener, and won there by Takisuma Ogama after red mist blinded his opponent.

name: MLW True North Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Taken from DT Richman and Ron Rivers by Ryan Winters and Nemo Chan-El, who kept it by disqualification at Maplemania 2.
notes: Billed as the True North Tag Team titles on the promotion's 2001 broadcast; no document shows whether it continues the 1999 World Tag Team Championship or the 1999 True North Championship.
